claim: Fresh local automated normal +hold/+attack production-command/model acceptance in real private PostgreSQL with actual PvP sessions and durable checkpoint/rebuilds; session transport and initial fixture setup are separate.
scope: two confirmed offensive-hook gaps repaired in one damage consumer
current per-item status, normal player-flow and engine tests, documentation and lifecycle CI

rules.boost: Matching-type base power int(power * 1.2); no nonmatching boost or cumulative repeated-use boost/consumption. Legal ability/item power results compose in order.
rules.rounding: PF2 integer base-power and damage pipeline retained; verify the independent floored formula using actual emitted level/attack/defense/STAB/effectiveness/roll. Final HP loss is not assumed to be exactly 1.2 times baseline.
rules.variance: Reset real Random(771) and ordinary random seed per paired turn; all measured damage traces require noncritical hits and matching controls. No accuracy/damage/callback success is mocked.
rules.suppression: Existing EffectContext.item disables owned item effects under Magic Room, Embargo, Klutz and explicit item suppression without removing ownership. Magic Room toggle restores boost.
rules.removal: Normal +hold removal/replacement returns the previous held copy to the bag. Real Knock Off clears runtime/saved held state and remains empty after two rebuilds; it does not return a bag copy.
rules.checkpoint: Every item has a matching action restored twice while queued; all-item Magic Room, Embargo and Knock Off contexts are also rebuilt twice before attacking.
rules.native_ability_composition: Native Sand Force Gigalith retains Rock Incense in clear weather (80 to 96) and composes Sand Force then incense in sandstorm (80 to 104 to 124). Native Unnerve Tyranitar is sand-immune and avoids residual HP or automatic-weather confounds. Sand state is rebuilt twice in each paired run.
rules.unchanged: Existing dex definitions/metadata/callback multipliers, genetic stats, identity, placement, inventory quantities during attacks, breeding and unrelated field/battle fixes

confirmed_defect.trigger: A normally equipped incense user attacks during Magic Room/Embargo or with native Klutz
confirmed_defect.before: Raw held ownership still invokes onBasePower, yielding 108 instead of unheld/suppressed 90 (96 instead of 80 for Rock).
confirmed_defect.cause: engine._apply_move_damage read owner.item/held_item directly before invoking offensive item hooks
confirmed_defect.repair: Read EffectContext.item(owner) at that consumer; no new suppression state or incense multiplier

native_composition_defect.fresh_reproduction: Native Sand Force Gigalith, legal Power Gem and ordinary +hold/+attack yielded power 80 both unheld and with Rock Incense in clear weather.
native_composition_defect.cause: An ability onBasePower result skipped the item hook, even when the ability returned unchanged power.
native_composition_defect.repair: Apply the numeric ability result, then invoke the effective held-item hook on that power. Test no-op and active Sand Force separately; callback multipliers remain unchanged.

public_reproduction.postgres_environment: PF2_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN must explicitly select a disposable PostgreSQL database; the suite creates/drops its own isolated schema.

raw_walkthroughs_note: Full SQL/model/runtime snapshots retained locally in ignored .codex-artifacts/incense-20261022/player-flows.json; published walkthroughs retain effect-relevant SQL/runtime, complete bag/placement/move rows and captured outputs.

setup_and_cleanup.fixture_setup: Tagged ordinary User owners; gapped canonical slot 3; native level-50 Mew with legal Psychic/Power Gem/Energy Ball/Surf plus Swift/Magic Room/Safeguard, real fixed IV/EV/nature and helper-calculated HP/stats; real bag copies granted separately as fixture setup. Opposing bulky Mew uses legal Safeguard/Embargo/Knock Off; native Klutz Swoobat and Dark Umbreon provide controls. Native Sand Force Gigalith uses legal Power Gem/Sandstorm. The additional sand-only Unnerve Tyranitar target is assigned harmless Safeguard as fixture setup to avoid residual HP confounds; its move learnability is not an acceptance claim.
setup_and_cleanup.transport_adapters: Capture session output and object search; normal parser, +hold ownership/inventory service, +attack choices/queue, complete PvP BattleSession turn lifecycle, real dex item callbacks, durable state and SQL writes execute unchanged. Only existing debug logging and seeded randomness are enabled for observations.
setup_and_cleanup.expected_failures: Psychic immunity on Umbreon is expected; repeated harmless Safeguard can correctly have no effect. Faster opposing Mew applies Embargo before the holder sets Safeguard. Compact dex identifiers are compared by normalized identity, not changed to create a boost.
setup_and_cleanup.cleanup: Isolated schemas removed and public tables empty; private task cluster stopped. No existing game database, human character, service or migration runner used.

preliminary_diagnosis: Initial 38-case run: 21 failures comprised eleven confirmed suppression failures (five Magic Room, five Embargo, one native Klutz) and ten fixture-only compact-name comparisons (five itemdex and five runtime names).
Fresh five-case diagnosis independently reproduced Magic Room/Embargo/Klutz power leakage with identical damage controls before the consumer repair.

After the repair and normalized naming, all 38 PostgreSQL cases passed. Initial unit fixtures required the correct Action import and real dex move types rather than the generic helper Normal default; these were setup errors, not further mechanics defects.

The suppression-only build passed 38 PostgreSQL cases, 20 engine regressions, 790 focused tests and two full orders (4655 passed / 4014 skipped). A new native-holder source concern justified an extra fresh ordinary-command reproduction: Sand Force Gigalith showed Rock Incense power 80 instead of 96. The superseded runner was stopped; its manifest/logs/receipts remain in suppression-only-verification/.

Added sequential ability/item composition in the same consumer, two native PostgreSQL cases and two engine regressions. Native clear-weather/sandstorm cases and all 22 engine regressions passed before the final freeze. The complete final acceptance reruns all affected suites and three full orders; no executable changes occurred after that freeze.
